Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

interaction noun

dealings between people

also interact, social interaction, contact (with people), dealings, have dealings with, social life

classical

Cic. Fam. 7.32.1: quōcum mihi est magnus ūsus
Cic. Rosc. Am. 15: domesticus ūsus et cōnsuētūdō (Lewis & Short)

ūsus, ūsūs m.

noun, fourth declension · Declension on Wiktionary

dealings, familiar contact between people

Its first sense is use or practice; of people, the intercourse and familiarity of those who deal with each other often (Lewis & Short): mihi cum eō magnus ūsus est, “I have a lot to do with him”. Often paired with cōnsuētūdō, being much together (see company).

Other words

  • commercium, commerciī n. — dealings, communication

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Aul. 4.4.4: quid tibi mēcum est commercī, senex? (Lewis & Short); Cic. Tusc. 5.66: commercium habēre cum Mūsīs (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    First trade, commerce; then any dealings or communication: mihi cum vostrīs lēgibus nihil est commercī, “I have nothing to do with your laws” (Plaut. Rud. 3.4.20, Lewis & Short).

  • congressus, congressūs m. — meeting, social contact (often plural)

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Lael. 87 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    A friendly meeting or conversation, in the plural social contact; also a hostile encounter, a clash (Lewis & Short). See meeting.

  • inter sē — with one another (for “interact”)

    phrase, with a verb: inter sē colloquī, inter sē dīligere · also used · classical

    Latin says “interact” with a verb of what is done and inter sē, “with one another” (see each other).

Examples

  • quōcum mihi est magnus ūsus

    with whom I have a great deal to doCic. Fam. 7.32.1

See also relationship, company, associate, each other, meeting, society.
